facts.topic: Venetian poker suite rates (official rate tied to poker play)
facts.quote: These rates will start as low as $119 and $209 and can be higher. Future rates are only provided out to a maximum of 150 days from the current date. Rates are subject to qualifying poker play and availability based on hotel occupancy. ... There is a $55 resort fee per night stayed. ... During your stay, you will be required to play six hours of active live cash gameplay or buy in to a $300 or higher tournament for each night stayed. ... For any nights you fail to complete these requirements, your nightly suite rate will be adjusted to the prevailing rate.
facts.establishes: The only room rate an official Venetian page states in numbers: a published poker-suite rate starting at $119 (and $209) per night for a Luxury King Suite at single/double occupancy, with a $55 nightly resort fee, conditional on six hours of cash play or one $300+ tournament buy-in per night stayed, qualifying play completed before 2 a.m. on the last night. This is a published 'starting at' floor, not a dated quote for a specific stay, so it is kept as a rate-floor scenario in the dated log and never as the trip's confirmed hotel cost.
facts.result: unchanged (page title reads '2026 Special Suite Rates')
facts.caveat: not a dated availability quote; qualifying play required; unmet nights revert to the prevailing rate

facts.topic: Venetian parking (self-parking rates and poker-player waiver)
facts.quote: The daily fee for registered hotel guests is $20/day, seven days a week. For non-hotel guests, the fee is $20/day Monday - Thursday, and $25/day Friday - Sunday. Valet parking is $40/day. ... Players in the poker room who play three hours or more in tournament or cash games will receive complimentary self-parking for the day. Players must visit a supervisor at the end of their session to confirm qualifications.
facts.establishes: Parking is a real, published cost line for the trip: $20 per day self-parking for a registered hotel guest, $25 on Friday-Sunday for a non-guest, $40 valet; and a tournament player who plays three hours or more gets that day's self-parking free (supervisor confirmation required). A day's tournament entry almost always exceeds three hours, so a player who parks each day and plays 3 h+ pays $0 parking at this property.

facts.topic: Caesars Palace / Horseshoe daily tournament structure
facts.quote: At Caesars Palace, the daily schedule runs like clockwork. You will find four No-Limit Hold'em tournaments each day at 10 a.m., 2 p.m., 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. Every event carries a $100 buy-in, starts you with 20,000 chips, and features a $1,000 guaranteed prize pool. facts.establishes: Four Caesars Palace starts per day, $100 buy-in, 20,000 chips, $1,000 guaranteed, 20-minute levels and an optional $50 add-on at the first break. The page is an official Caesars editorial page dated July 17, 2026; it publishes no event numbers and no per-day calendar, so these rows carry no date.

facts.topic: Caesars Palace resort fee (official corporate disclaimer)
facts.quote: Room reservations are subject to a daily resort fee between $45-$60 plus applicable tax. Resort fees are waived for Diamond and Seven Stars.
facts.establishes: The official Caesars statement is a RANGE ($45-$60 per night plus tax), not a single fee, and it is waived for Diamond and Seven Stars members. A range cannot be multiplied into a stay total, so the site publishes the range and leaves the 'true nightly cost' for Caesars blank with a flag instead of picking a number. Note the range is wider than the $45-$50 wording some secondary caches still show.
facts.result: range confirmed live; no single value publishable

facts.topic: Clark County transient lodging tax and what is taxed
facts.quote: Resort hotel within primary gaming corridor | 12.5% | 0.88% | 13.38% ... (17) 'Rent' (a) Means the amount charged for a sleeping room/space ... including the following, regardless of whether separately stated: (i) Charges that would normally be part of an all inclusive room rate, such as, but not limited to, payment processing fees, check-in fees, accommodation fees, facility fees, access fees, charges for additional guests, late check-out fees, and utility surcharges
facts.establishes: 13.38% is the combined transient lodging tax for a resort hotel inside the primary gaming corridor (12.5% + 0.88%), and the ordinance's definition of 'rent' includes separately stated accommodation, facility and access fees - which is why this site taxes the room rate AND the mandatory resort fee. The document is the ordinance as published for the Board hearing; the rate schedule was effective 2017-03-01 and the page warns rates may be changed by the jurisdictions, so the multiplier is stated with that caveat.
